fields.why: The DMS Thickener discharge controller 720-FIC-2134 & 720-DIC-2134 Currently runs in auto to flow 720-FIC-2134. Can’t be run in remote, as the controller does not consider the increasing rake torque required to be changed to auto flow to get rake torque under control.
fields.design:
Introduction of a max selector between density and rake torque that will adjust the flow SP to slowly bring rake torque down instead of rapidly emptying the hopper.
- Addition of a torque controller 720-NIC-2135
- Addition of Max selector between 720-NIC-2135 and 720-DIC-2134 that links to current control logic of flow controller.
- Label the 720-NIC-2135 check box Rake Torque
- Label the 720-DIC-2134 check box Density
- Addition of H and HH SW points on 720-NI-2135 at 20% and 25%
- Each switch point is the trigger for a bias increase for how much extra flow the torque controller demands
- Bias setpoints: 20% = +5m3/hr and >25% = +10m3/h
- Bias >20% +5m3hr until torque < 16% (then -5m3hr) or torque >25% then +10m3hr until torque < 21% (then back to just +5m3hr)
- The bias should reduce process upsets and allow density controller to still be the fundamentally main controller.
- Have bias values and triggers adjustable through metallurgy login.

Rake torque controller demand of flow controller (720-FIC-2134) to be 10m3/hr higher than that of the density controller. This will allow the rake torque to come down.
- PV = 720-NI-2135 Instrument Scaled Value
- SP = 20% rake torque
- CV = 720-DIC-2134 CV + Bias
- Have process off conditions align with 720-DIC-2134
fields.impact: Thickener discharge increases gradually as rake torque rises instead of CROs emptying the hopper manually.
